title: Touch Projection
shortDescription: Any wall becomes a living illustration: visitors touch the projected scene and it answers with animations, sounds, and stories, turning a plain surface into an explorable world.
longDescription: A projection turns a wall, a room corner, or an entire space into an illustrated story that reacts to touch. Visitors tap a drawing and it comes alive: machines start moving, characters react, hidden details open up with text, images, or sound. Physical props such as peepholes, tubes, or objects built into the wall can extend the scene and reveal content of their own. Because the surface is projected, it can cover large, irregular areas without screens, and the illustrations, stories, and languages are fully configurable, from a product journey in a brand space to a learning wall in a museum. BRDGE handles the interaction logic, scene management, and journey, leaderboard, and data links end to end.

highlights.title: A Wall Full of Surprises
highlights.description: Every drawing is a possible discovery, so visitors keep exploring to see what reacts next. Curiosity does the work, and the space holds attention far longer than a printed wall.

highlights.title: Big Surfaces, No Screens
highlights.description: Projection covers whole walls, corners, and odd shapes at a fraction of the cost of large displays, and it blends into the architecture instead of looking like a screen.

highlights.title: Physical Meets Digital
highlights.description: Peepholes, tubes, buttons, or real products built into the wall become part of the story, giving visitors something to look into, pull, or touch beyond the projection itself.

highlights.title: Layers to Unlock
highlights.description: Add hidden scenes that open after several touches, a seek-and-find challenge across the wall, timed shows that take over the whole surface, or a mode where several visitors trigger a joint finale.

highlights.title: Draw Any World
highlights.description: Tell how chocolate is made in a factory shop, how a city grows in a museum, how a product travels from field to shelf, or how a season changes in a festive edition.

highlights.title: See What Draws People In
highlights.description: Add a data layer that counts touches per hotspot, sessions, and dwell time, so the client sees which parts of the story attract visitors and which can be improved.

highlights.title: Part of the Story Route
highlights.description: Pair with Spatial Mediaguide to continue the story on visitors' phones, with Cloud Content Management to update texts and languages, or with Journey Manager to make the wall one stop on a longer route.
